request.description: Edits a draft's content or notes; issues are recomputed. `content`: `priority` (lower runs first, default 100; ties by key), `when` (a condition on `lead.*` attributes such as `lead.segment`, `lead.category`, `lead.state` (GST code), `lead.city_id`, `lead.pincode`, `lead.amount_paise`, `lead.source`, `lead.campaign`, `lead.language`, `lead.urgency`, `lead.quality_score`, `lead.flags`, or on any dictionary attribute; omit to match every lead), `strategy` (`round_robin`, `least_loaded`, `weighted`, `sticky`, `broadcast`; `manual` and `pool` leave the lead for ops), `offers` (how many CAs a `broadcast` offers at once), `maxOffers` (offers per lead before ops takes over, default 5), `pool` (`kinds`, `levels`, `organizationIds`; `requireServiceArea` and `requireCapabilities` default true, `requireLanguage` false), `weights` per partner level (`new`, `active`, `strategic`; defaults 1, 2, 3) and `sla` (`acceptHours` default 4, `firstContactHours` default 24). Staff only. Routing rules are versioned config (same lifecycle as question sets): an ops lead makes, a different staff member approves in Change Requests, then it is published. Reading needs config read access; making, publishing and retiring need config maker access for routing rules (ops lead, super admin).
